The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content: "111 :     private static Map cDateInstanceCache = new HashMap(7);"

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does
  - It sets the default Locale to US, then obtains:
    - format1 = getDateInstance(FULL, Locale.GERMANY) with an explicit locale.
    - format2 = getDateInstance(FULL) with no locale (uses default = US).
  - It then changes the default Locale to GERMANY and obtains:
    - format3 = getDateInstance(FULL) with no locale (now should use default = GERMANY).
  - It expects format2’s locale to be US, format3’s locale to be GERMANY, and format2 != format3.

- Relevant implementation (FastDateFormat)
  - getDateInstance(int) delegates to getDateInstance(style, null, null). [lines 233–235]
  - The core cache lookup happens in getDateInstance(int, TimeZone, Locale): [lines 279–306]
    - It builds a cache key starting with the style (Integer).
    - If timeZone != null: key = Pair(key, timeZone). [281–283]
    - If locale != null: key = Pair(key, locale). [285–287]
    - Then it looks up cDateInstanceCache with that key. [290]
    - Only after the cache lookup, if locale == null, it sets locale = Locale.getDefault(). [292–294]
    - It then builds the formatter and creates the FastDateFormat with that resolved locale, and puts it into the cache under the previously built key (which did not include the default locale if locale was null). [295–303]
  - getLocale() simply returns mLocale. [953–955]
  - The same pattern exists in getDateTimeInstance(...): locale is added to the key only if non-null, and locale is defaulted after cache lookup. [458–486]

- How the bug manifests, step by step
  1. With default Locale = US, the call format2 = getDateInstance(FULL) arrives at getDateInstance(style, null, null) with locale == null and timeZone == null.
     - The cache key is built as just Integer(style) because locale is null (so the locale is not added to the key). [279–287]
     - Cache miss occurs (first call), then locale is set to Locale.getDefault() (US). [292–294]
     - A FastDateFormat is created with locale = US and stored in cDateInstanceCache under the key Integer(style) (which contains no locale component). [296–303]
  2. The default Locale is changed to GERMANY.
  3. The call format3 = getDateInstance(FULL) again comes in with locale == null and timeZone == null.
     - The same cache key Integer(style) is built (no locale included). [279–287]
     - The cache lookup now hits the entry created when the default was US. [290–305]
     - That previously cached FastDateFormat has mLocale = US (because that was the default when it was created), so format3.getLocale() returns US instead of GERMANY.
     - format2 and format3 are the same cached instance, so format2 != format3 fails.
  4. format1 = getDateInstance(FULL, Locale.GERMANY) explicitly specifies a locale; the implementation includes the locale in the key when it is non-null, so format1 is distinct and correctly reports Locale.GERMANY. [285–287]

- Root cause
  - In getDateInstance(int, TimeZone, Locale) (and similarly in getDateTimeInstance(...)), the cache key is constructed without including the default locale when the locale parameter is null. The locale is only resolved to Locale.getDefault() after the cache key has been built and the cache has been consulted.
  - As a result, calls made before and after a change to the default Locale use the same key and return the same cached instance, even though the effective locale should differ.

- Additional note
  - The same pattern also exists for timeZone: the key only includes the timeZone when it is non-null, while the FastDateFormat constructor defaults a null timeZone to TimeZone.getDefault(). This implies a similar potential bug if the default time zone changes. However, the failing test specifically exercises the locale behavior.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

FastDateFormat.getDateInstance(int, TimeZone, Locale)
FastDateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(int, int, TimeZone, Locale)
